title: Brute Force and CAPTCHA Handling
description: Approaches for hydra/burp in CAPTCHA scenarios
detail:
No CAPTCHA: Burp Intruder (pitchfork username + password) / hydra http-post-form
CAPTCHA scenarios:
1. Echoed: the code appears in the response/frontend base64 → script reads the code and replays
2. Not invalidated: one CAPTCHA can be reused multiple times → brute force with a fixed code
3. Recognizable: ddddocr (Python library; can quickly solve common 4-character CAPTCHAs locally)
4. Universal code: source leak shows an empty-value bypass in === comparison
5. Front-end validation only: brute force directly at the API layer
Rate-limit bypass: vary XFF, change username case (WordPress pitfall), distribute parameters
Brute-force discipline: try a small dictionary first (top 1000) → stop immediately on a hit and record a cred fact → move to the next target (time in assessments is more valuable than a single password)
ssh/rdp: hydra -L users -P pass T ssh; prioritize cewl-generated targeted lists.
